w: Second-largest of the Lerins Islands, Saint-Honorat lies about 1.6 kilometres off Cannes: a strip of land roughly 1.5 kilometres long and 400 metres wide. It has been home to a community of monks since the 5th century, a monastic presence a short crossing from the Croisette's crowds.
s: Monk-inhabited island a mile off the Croisette
_facts: Second-largest of the Lerins Islands
About 1.6 km off Cannes; roughly 1.5 km long, 400 m wide
Community of monks resident since the 5th century

n: Monastère fortifié de l'abbaye de Lérins
w: On Saint-Honorat's southern shore, this fortified monastery was begun in the late 11th century to defend both island and abbey from raiders. Its stout walls doubled as a refuge for the monks who had lived here since the 5th century. Listed as a historic monument in 1840, it still stands watch over the Lerins channel.
s: An 11th-century fortress built to guard monks
_facts: Construction began late 11th century
Built on the southern coast of Saint-Honorat to protect the island and abbey
Listed as a Monument historique in 1840

w: Set in a 16th-century mill in the hill town of Mougins, this restaurant made its name under founding chef Roger Verge's 'Cuisine du Soleil'. By 2009 it held four Michelin knives-and-forks; back in 1977 a young Alain Ducasse worked here as an assistant, learning the Provencal cooking he later made his own.
s: A 16th-century mill where Ducasse learned to cook
_facts: Housed in a 16th-century mill (moulin) in Mougins
Founding chef Roger Verge made its name with 'Cuisine du Soleil'
Rated four knives-and-forks in the Michelin Guide as of 2009
Alain Ducasse worked here as an assistant in 1977

w: Built in the 1880s for James Bland, this Cannes property passed in 1925 to Danae and Marino Vagliano, who expanded the house and laid out its garden by 1928. The family sold up in 1961; a new house replaced the old one in 1964, but the garden survived intact and was listed as a historic monument in 1990.
s: A Cannes garden that outlived two houses
_facts: First house built in the 1880s for James Bland
Bought by Danae and Marino Vagliano in 1925; expanded and gardened through 1928
Sold in 1961; a new 1964 house replaced the original
The garden alone is listed as a historic monument (since 1990)

w: Built in 1928 for Marcelle Aron, widow of First World War veteran Jacques Isidore Gompel, this Cannes mansion was designed by Georges-Henri Pingusson and Paul Furiet, its garden added the following year. Aron sold up in 1935; the house has been a listed historic monument since 1994.
_facts: Built 1928 for Marcelle Aron, widow of WWI veteran Jacques Isidore Gompel
Designed by Georges-Henri Pingusson and Paul Furiet
Garden added 1929; house sold in 1935
Listed as a historic monument since 1994

w: American architect Barry Dierks built this Modernist villa on the Golfe-Juan shore in 1932 for actress Maxine Elliott. Winston Churchill was a regular guest through the 1930s; Prince Ali Khan bought the place in 1948 and married Rita Hayworth here the following year.
s: Where Rita Hayworth married a prince, 1949
_facts: Modernist villa built 1932 by architect Barry Dierks for actress Maxine Elliott
On the Golfe-Juan shore at Vallauris
Churchill was a regular guest 1934-1940
Prince Ali Khan bought it in 1948 and married Rita Hayworth there in 1949

w: Painter Jean-Gabriel Domergue built this Cannes house in 1926, laying out its garden over the following decade. It ran as a museum to his work from 1962 to 1973, then became a City of Cannes venue, listed as a historic monument since 1990 - and the room where the Film Festival jury meets to choose its winners.
s: Where the Cannes Film Festival jury picks a winner
_facts: Built 1926 for painter Jean-Gabriel Domergue; garden laid out 1926-1936
Ran as a Domergue museum 1962-1973, then an official City of Cannes venue
Listed as a historic monument since 1990
The Cannes Film Festival jury meets here to choose the winners

w: This Mougins gallery opened in July 2021 on the site of a photography museum that had closed in 2018, its rehabilitation funded jointly by the town and the regional government. Its inaugural show featured Isabel Munoz, and under artistic director Francois Cheval it has kept the village's photographic tradition alive.
s: A photography museum's second life in Mougins
_facts: Opened July 2021 in Mougins
Occupies the site of the former Andre Villiers photography museum, closed 2018
Financed by the municipality and the regional government
Inaugural exhibition by Isabel Munoz; artistic director Francois Cheval

n: Female Artists of the Mougins Museum
w: Founded by Christian Levett in June 2024 on the site of the former Mougins Museum of Classical Art, FAMM is dedicated solely to women artists - over 100 works by some 80 of them, ranging from Impressionism to contemporary practice, in the hill village above Cannes.
s: A museum for women artists only, opened 2024
_facts: Opened June 2024, founded by Christian Levett
Occupies the former site of the Mougins Museum of Classical Art
Over 100 artworks by roughly 80 female artists worldwide
Spans Impressionism to Contemporary art
